task.title: M4: Experimental Map view: graph folders with treemap-sized file boxes
task.description:
The treemap is hard to navigate: folder targets are small and file blocks cannot be manipulated like graph nodes. Add an experimental fourth view, Map, that combines the two: folders are rendered as the graph view's expandable and collapsible compound nodes (double-click, Expand all / Collapse all, Fit, Re-layout, cycles, tooltips, right-click Hide), but files inside an expanded folder are drawn as rectangles whose area is proportional to code lines (sqrt scaling, sensible min and max sides, label inside when it fits) and colored by the same complexity or churn scale and legend as the treemap, with a Complexity | Churn toggle. A collapsed folder's box area is proportional to the folder's total code. Edges are drawn with the same arrows as the graph view and can be toggled off and on with a Show edges checkbox (positions are kept when toggling). File boxes and folders are draggable; children stay inside their folder compound. The treemap and graph views stay as they are; the map view is a separate option in the header switcher, with view=map, mode=, and edges= in the hash.

Acceptance criteria:
- On Capacitor and workbook the Map view opens collapsed to top-level folders sized by total code, with edges; Expand all shows every file as a sized, colored box; a 2000-line file is visibly larger than a 50-line one.
- Complexity | Churn toggle recolors boxes and the legend matches the treemap's.
- Show edges off hides all edges without moving nodes; on restores them.
- Dragging a file box moves it and keeps it inside its folder; dragging a folder moves its children.
- Tooltips show the treemap's file metrics; right-click Hide works; cycles are highlighted when edges are shown.
- The existing Treemap, Graph, and Compare views are unchanged and the headless Chrome check on both repos has no console errors.
